title: Data reference (URF pointer at a Reference Data Layer)
description: The canonical in-field reference to shared, governed data (UDLM ADR-012) — a field points at a Reference Data Layer instead of inlining a copy. The shape is a URF reference string (identifier-scheme §9), not an object: `uuid/<v4>[@version][?reference_data_type==<kind>]`. It MUST resolve to an ACTIVE `layer` record with layer_type: reference_data whose reference_data_type equals the kind the reference declares (docs/spec/foundations/layering-and-versioning.md §3.7). Referential integrity is enforced by registry/tools/validate.py (check_data_references): a dangling uuid, a kind mismatch, or a pin naming a version other than the resolved one is a hard failure — invalid edges resolve deterministically, never silently. A schema that lets a field be either a reference or an inline value $refs this $defs/data_reference on one branch of a oneOf.

data_reference.description: A pointer at IMMUTABLE reference-data (DCM ADR-012), written as a URF reference (identifier-scheme §9): `uuid/<v4>[@version][?reference_data_type==<kind>]`. The uuid path is AUTHORITATIVE — resolution uses only it, and a reference_data layer is an immutable record, so a change is a NEW record with its own uuid linked by `supersedes` (never an in-place edit). The pin axis carries the version; the query term carries the expected kind, which the resolved layer must match. The former object (ref_uuid/ref_name/ref_version/reference_data_type/residency/resolving_authority) is REMOVED because the URL SUBSUMES every one of its parts: uuid and version are axes, the kind is a query term, and `resolving_authority` — ADR-038 §10's routing root, *who* resolves the reference — is the URL's authority axis (`//state.mn/uuid/<v4>`), which keeps that root distinct from `residency`, the attribute you resolve *to* (a field on the target record, filterable as `?residency==state.mn`). The advisory `ref_name` is simply dropped — it duplicated what resolution returns (DRV-001: the model does not store what it can derive), and its drift-check existed only to police that duplicate. Distinct from a resource Reference (common-elements §2.5), which points at a resource rather than reference-data.
